quandoUsar: The initial setup of an account or workspace, with three to eight steps that can be done in any order.
Steps the interface itself performs: with `actionLabel` and an asynchronous `onAction`, the button shows loading, marks the step when done, and shows the error message if it fails.
A welcome card the user can collapse (`defaultHidden`, `onHiddenChange`) and which, at the end, swaps `title` for `doneTitle`.
quandoEvitar: Use `stepper` when the order is mandatory, such as in a checkout where one step unlocks the next.
Use `todo-list` to show an AI agent's plan advancing on its own, with the user checking nothing.
Use `checkbox` for a simple task list, with no details or per-item actions.

teclado.acao: With focus on a step's title, moves to the previous or next title, wrapping around at the end of the list.
Moves to the title of the first or last step in the list.
On the title, opens or closes the step's details; on the circle, checks or unchecks; on the action, runs `onAction`.

acessibilidade: Each circle is a button with `role="checkbox"` and `aria-checked`, named by the step's title; the title opens the details with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
The ring is `role="progressbar"` (“N of M steps done”) and a `role="status"` region announces each step done or undone; the `onAction` error appears with `role="alert"`.
When a focused step collapses, focus moves to the action of the next open step, and unchecking in the completed group moves focus to the circle of the step that came back.
movimento: On checking, the circle fills from the center and the checkmark draws itself; the title gets a strikethrough that crosses the line and, after 0.72 s, the step collapses into the completed group.

Rows and panels open and close their height with a no-overshoot spring; the ring fills with each step, the numbers turn in the direction of the change, and a checkmark appears in the ring when everything is finished.
With “reduce motion”, heights change immediately with a short fade, strikethrough and fill appear without transition, and the action button's spinner stops.
responsivo: In a card narrower than 380 px (container query), the hide button shows only the arrow and keeps its spoken name.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/onboarding-checklist/onboarding-checklist`. It is uncontrolled: pass `defaultCompleted` with the ids already done and save progress from `onCompletedChange`.
In `onAction`, return a Promise: resolving marks the step; throwing `new Error("mensagem")` keeps the step open with the message. Without `actionLabel`, the step is only checked by hand.
The fixed texts (“Setup progress”, “Hide”, “completed”, the default error message) are in English; translate them in the copied file. Each step needs a stable `id`.
